issuerVisibility.note: [S] the verifier learns which issuer; bits = log2(number of equally sized issuers)

epochVisibility.note: [S] the epoch is shared by every holder of the issuer; it reveals at most which anchor interval the presentation fell in, which the verifier already knows from time

pathFetchPublished.note: [S] published-tree mode: every wallet downloads the same blob

perHolderEpochTargeting.note: [S] registry cadence caps epochs at one per interval; with published trees the issuer cannot tell who presents in an epoch, so this only partitions presentations by hour

refusalKinds.note: [S] observation model DECISIONS D-026 (the caller of the wallet sees the refusal reason and timing): for a request that passes the request-level checks, a revoked credential or one not yet in the anchored epoch is refused with one generic anchorMatches refusal, differently from one that does not satisfy the predicate or has expired (predicateHolds); only holders who cannot present are affected. Requests with a non-standard threshold, a non-current date or a type outside the allow-list are refused before any credential-dependent work (routes TP-a, TP-c, TP-d, SD-b, SD-d, SD-f, SD-g, TY-c).

dateLogAcrossVerifiers.note: [S] review round 2 VRA-2: the wallet answers one date per window across all verifiers, so a verifier asking the other date within the window after midnight learns that the holder answered some verifier for the first date (DECISIONS D-027)

allowListMembership.note: [S] review round 2 VRA-6: typeAllowed and typeHeld refuse differently, so a verifier can learn whether a type is on the wallet's allow-list (the list itself, not the credentials held beyond the D-018 bound)

midnightTolerance.note: [S] share of the day in which the wallet accepts two dates (the previous date only in the first WALLET_CLOCK_SKEW_SEC after UTC midnight, never a future date; DECISIONS D-017); within any 2 x WALLET_CLOCK_SKEW_SEC window the wallet answers one date only, so a verifier gets at most one of the two answers per visit
